text:
alex: Heads-up — we started seeing intermittent 503s hitting interface endpoints for S3 in us-west-2. Affected requests are coming from pods in az-b and az-c only, az-a looks fine. suspecting DNS/route propagation mismatch after yesterday's route table swap.

mira: ack. any changes pushed to the VPC endpoint terraform?

alex: yes, we moved some subnets between route table A->B last night to rebalance NAT egress paths. I can see the endpoint ENIs in both AZs but targets in az-b show RSTs and the DNS sometimes resolves to the private ip in az-a.

sam: hmm that sounds like stale split-horizon / cache issue at nodes? can you paste the output of `dig +short mybucket.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com` from an affected node and from a working node?

alex: here — from pod in az-b (failing):
```
10.0.11.23
```
from az-a (working):
```
10.0.3.7
```

mira: ok so DNS returns different ENI IPs per AZ. but traffic from az-b is trying to hit the az-a IP and getting blackholed when local SGs/route don't allow cross-az. can you `ip route get 10.0.3.7` on the node?

alex: ran it, shows next-hop via eni-0a1b2c and diff src. also saw tcpdump showing SYN -> no SYN-ACK then RST from local NAT.

infra-bot: detected change: route-table association updated for subnet subnet-0b12345 by terraform-apply (user: infra-automation).

sam: two quick checks: 1) vpc endpoint policy/enableDnsHostnames + enableDnsSupport still on? 2) are there any route table propagation delays with the TGW? we've had the TGW route table controller take ~30-60s to converge but this sounds longer.

alex: both DNS flags are on. TGW not involved here, pure tenant VPC. propagation delay looks >7m.

mira: can you also check the endpoint network interface owner-id and confirm SGs on the ENI allow intra-VPC traffic from the subnet CIDR? I've seen ENI owner mismatches when endpoints recreated by automation (owner aws:vpce vs our account-level ENI tag mismatch).

alex: owner is correct (aws:vpce). SGs look permissive for TCP 443 from the subnets. but flow logs show `REJECT` for traffic to 10.0.3.7 from 10.0.11.0/24. digging into NACLs now.

josh: tagging note — when infra-automation recreated the endpoint yesterday it made a new interface in az-b but left the old private hosted zone A record pointing to the az-a IP; route53 resolver cache on our nodes cached the old answer. Need to clear node DNS cache and make sure VPC resolver endpoint updates.

sam: actions: (1) clear coredns cache on nodes in az-b (`kubectl -n kube-system delete pods -l k8s-app=kube-dns`) (2) confirm route table association for subnet-0b is to RT-B and that RT-B has local route to the az-b ENI, (3) check NACLs for ephemeral port denies, (4) add short TTL override for the private hosted zone record to force faster refresh while we investigate.

alex: doing (1) + (4) now. updating route table and NACL checks after.

mira: if this persists after DNS flush, we should temporarily attach an AZ-local endpoint variant (s3 interface endpoint in az-b) and update a routing rule to prefer local ENI. that buys time without sweeping infra.

alex: update — coredns pods restarted, dig from az-b now resolves to 10.0.11.21 (az-b ENI). requests succeed again. looks like node-level DNS cache + private hosted zone TTL caused ~10m of split answers.

sam: nice. followups: add automation test to ensure private hosted zone records are updated atomically when endpoints are replaced, and reduce TTL to 30s after future endpoint rollouts. also add an alert for cross-az ENI hit ratio > 5% for interface endpoints.

ajosh: noted, will open infra ticket and add to oncall runbook. :white_check_mark:
